statement.p: Suppose a curve is traced by the parametric equations x = 3 \big(\sin(t)+\cos(t)\big)
as t runs from 0 to \pi. At what point (x,y) on this curve is the tangent line horizontal?

static.solution:
0 = \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt} = \frac{9\cdot 2\cos(t)\sin(t) - 18\cos(t)}{3 \big(\cos(t)-\sin(t)\big)}.
If this fraction is zero then its numerator is zero 0=dy/dt = 18\cos(t)\big(\sin(t)-1\big) so \cos(t)=0 or \sin(t)=1. Since 0\leq t \leq \pi it follows that t = \frac{\pi}{2} is the only possibility. It works because the denominator of the fraction \displaystyle \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt} is not zero when t=\pi/2, so there really is a horizontal tangent when t=\pi/2.
Plug t=\pi/2 into the parametric equations to obtain x,y-coordinates of the point where the horizontal line is tangent x= 3 \left(\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)+\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\right)= 3 and y = 29 - 9\cos^2\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) - 18\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 29 - 0 - 18 = 11.
